mainTopic: Does the בכור get a double portion of growth in the estate that happened after the father died? The view of רבי versus the רבנן, and the רבנן's source from the word 'giving' (a gift).
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining a ברייתא about a rented cow that grew after the father's death. Because the brothers spent nothing on it, the growth 'came by itself,' so the בכור takes a double portion. The גמרא says this ברייתא follows רבי, who gives the בכור double on growth that comes by itself but not on growth the orphans produce. The רבנן give no double portion on any growth after death. רבי's view also covers debts: the בכור takes double on money owed to the father and pays double on the father's debts, but he may give up both. Each side then brings its source from the same פסוק. The רבנן read 'לתת לו' as calling the double share a gift, which covers only what the father held. רבי reads 'פי שנים' as linking the extra share to a regular share. Each side explains what the other word teaches. רב פפא then shows that everyone agrees when the item only gets bigger, and that they argue only when it changes form. Finally, רבי חייא rules that a judge who follows either view has ruled validly.

steps.title: The rented cow's growth came by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the rented or leased cow in the ברייתא is also a case of growth that came on its own, because the brothers paid nothing to feed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, a cow that was leased or rented counts as growth that came by itself, since the brothers did not spend anything on its food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer about the ברייתא. It explains why the בכור takes a double portion even in the case of a rented cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether the growth came from the heirs' effort or money. The renter fed the cow, so the brothers lost nothing. That makes the growth 'by itself' and not something the orphans produced.

keyTerms.meaning: growth or improvement that comes by itself

phrases.english: So too, a leased or rented one
phrases.notes: This is the cow from the ברייתא that was rented out. The renter was the one feeding it.

phrases.english: the enhancement is coming by itself,
since they did not lose its food costs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section, explaining the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as self-generated growth
steps.terutzMaskana: A rented cow's growth counts as 'by itself' because the heirs spent nothing on it.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the ברייתא it has been explaining. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the בכור a double portion of growth that happened after the father's death. Not every תנא agrees with that, so the גמרא wants to know whose view it is.

phrases.english: Whose is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained the ברייתא, the גמרא asks who its author is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the ברייתא follows.

steps.title: It is רבי, who splits growth into two kinds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי. A ברייתא records that the תנא קמא gives the בכור no double portion of any growth after death. רבי gives it for growth that comes by itself, but not for growth the orphans produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: a בכור does not take a double portion of growth in the property after the father's death. רבי says: I say a בכור does take a double portion of growth that happened to the property after the father's death, but not of growth that the orphans produced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי. It brings a ברייתא showing that רבי disagrees with the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן give no double portion on any growth after death. רבי separates growth that happens by itself (like a calf being born) from growth the orphans created through work or money. Only the first kind gets a double portion, and that fits the rented cow from step 1.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two similar words: שֶׁשָּׁבְחוּ means the property grew by itself, while שֶׁהִשְׁבִּיחוּ means the orphans made it grow. רבי's whole view depends on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main מחלוקת of the סוגיא: whether growth after death is part of the בכור's double portion.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi, as it is taught:
A firstborn does not take a double portion
of the enhancement by which the property increased
after their father's death.
Rabbi says: I say:
a firstborn does take a double portion
of the enhancement by which the property increased
after their father's death,
but not of the enhancement that the orphans produced
after their father's death.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי, who gives a double portion for growth that came by itself.

steps.title: An inherited loan document: the בכור takes double
steps.stepSummary: If the brothers inherit a document showing that someone owed money to their father, the בכור takes a double portion when it is collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they inherited a promissory note, the firstborn takes a double portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling continues by applying רבי's idea to money that was owed to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money was not in the father's hands when he died; it was only owed to him. Even so, collecting it counts as growth that comes by itself and not through the orphans' work. So under רבי, the בכור gets double.

keyTerms.meaning: a promissory note, a written loan document

phrases.english: If they inherited a promissory note,
the firstborn takes a double portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי's rule to debts owed to the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור takes a double portion of a debt that was owed to the father.

steps.title: A debt against the estate: the בכור pays double, unless he opts out
steps.stepSummary: If a loan document is produced showing the father owed money, the בכור pays a double share. But if he gives up his double portion, he can refuse to pay double.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a promissory note came out against them, the firstborn pays a double portion. And if he says, 'I am not paying and I am not taking,' he is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: This step covers the opposite case, a debt that the father owed. It also gives the בכור a way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever takes a bigger share of the estate also carries a bigger share of its debts. Because the two go together, the בכור can give up the extra share and pay only like a regular brother.

keyTerms.meaning: came out against them (a claim was made against them)

phrases.english: If a promissory note came out against them,
the firstborn pays a double portion.
And if he says: 'I am not paying, and I am not taking,'
he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 4, a debt the father owed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור pays a double share of the father's debts, unless he gives up his double share of the estate.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי: the בכור takes double on growth that comes by itself and on debts owed to the father. He pays double on the father's debts, but he may give up both.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the extra share and the extra burden are linked, so he can turn down both together.

steps.title: What is the רבנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן hold that the בכור gets no double portion of any growth after the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the רבנן's view and asks for its source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think that anything added to the estate should be split by the usual rule. The גמרא wants to know what makes the רבנן limit the double portion to what the father had.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis (here, the תנא קמא who argues with רבי)

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the רבנן's position from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the רבנן's limit on the double portion.

steps.title: The double portion is called a gift
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'to give him a double portion,' so the תורה treats it like a gift. A gift only covers what the giver already holds, so the double portion only covers what was in the father's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says, 'to give him a double portion.' The Merciful One calls it a gift. Just as a gift only applies once it has reached the giver's hands, so too the firstborn's portion only applies once it has reached the father's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word 'to give' shows that the בכור's extra share works like a gift from the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only give what he actually has. Growth after death never reached the father, so it is not part of his 'gift' to the בכור. For the same reason, the רבנן also exclude debts owed to the father.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'To give him a double portion,'
the Merciful One called it a 'gift';
just as a gift applies only once it reaches his hand,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חֵלֶק בְּכוֹרָה – עַד דְּמָטְיָא לִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: so too the firstborn's portion applies only once it reaches his hand.
phrases.notes: 'His hand' means the father's: it has to be his before he dies.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'To give' makes the double portion a gift, which covers only what the father actually held.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: the double portion is a 'gift' from the father, so it only covers what was already his when he died, and not growth or money that came afterward.

steps.title: רבי's source: the double share is compared to a regular share
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from 'פי שנים' that the בכור's extra share works like a regular son's share. So it covers even property that never reached the father's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי says: the פסוק says 'a double portion.' This compares the בכור's portion to a regular son's portion. A regular son's portion applies even to what never reached the father's hands. So too, the בכור's portion applies even to what never reached the father's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just gave the רבנן's reason. Now it gives רבי's reason for letting the בכור take a double share of growth that came after the father died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'פי שנים' (literally 'two mouths') link the extra share to the ordinary share. A regular son clearly inherits things that came in after the father's death. Since the two shares are linked, the בכור's extra share covers those things too.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, linking two things so they follow the same rule
The extra share the בכור receives
Did not reach his hands (the father never held it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the direct counterpart to the רבנן's reasoning from 'לתת לו' in step 7. Each side builds its view on a different word in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: And רבי says: the verse says 'a double portion'
it compares the firstborn's portion to an ordinary portion;
just as the ordinary portion

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְטָא לִידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: applies even though it did not reach his hands,
phrases.notes: 'His hands' means the father's. It came in only after he died.

phrases.english: so too the firstborn's portion

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְטָא לִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: applies even though it did not reach his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's source after step 7 gave the רבנן's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'פי שנים' link the extra share to the ordinary share, so it covers property that came after the father's death.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'פי שנים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the רבנן: the words 'פי שנים' are also in the פסוק, so why don't you learn רבי's comparison from them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the רבנן too, isn't 'a double portion' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן. They also have the words 'פי שנים' in front of them, so what do they do with them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in a פסוק is expected to teach something. If the רבנן don't use 'פי שנים' to compare the two shares, they must use it for some other lesson. Otherwise they should agree with רבי.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too, isn't 'a double portion' written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי's source into a challenge against the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that the double share covers only what the father held
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן also read 'פי שנים,' which should create the comparison רבי learns from it.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'פי שנים' means both shares sit side by side
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'פי שנים' to teach that the בכור's two shares must be given to him as one connected plot.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase teaches that his shares are given to him on one border, joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. They do use 'פי שנים,' but for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read 'פי שנים' as telling us how the בכור's land is laid out: his regular share and his extra share sit next to each other, not in two separate places. Since the words are used up on this lesson, there is no comparison left to learn from them.

keyTerms.meaning: On one border, meaning in one connected piece of land

phrases.english: That is to give him [his shares] on one border.
phrases.notes: His two shares are joined into one plot instead of being split up.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פי שנים' must teach that the extra share is like a regular share.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, 'פי שנים' teaches that the two shares are given side by side.

steps.title: What does רבי do with 'לתת לו'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רבי: the words 'לתת לו' are also in the פסוק, and they suggest a gift, so why doesn't רבי follow them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי too, isn't 'to give him' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי the same way it challenged the רבנן. What does רבי do with the gift wording 'לתת לו'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the רבנן learned from 'לתת לו' that the double share is like a gift, which covers only what the father held. רבי must explain what else these words teach.

keyTerms.meaning: To give him, wording that makes the double share sound like a gift

phrases.english: And רבי too, isn't 'to give him' written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 9, now aimed at רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that the double share covers growth after death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לתת לו' makes the share a gift, and a gift covers only what the giver holds.

steps.title: רבי: 'לתת לו' lets the בכור refuse
steps.stepSummary: רבי uses 'לתת לו' to teach that since the double share is a gift, the בכור may turn it down. Then he also does not have to pay a double share of the father's debts.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase teaches that if he says 'I am not taking and I am not giving,' he is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי. The gift wording teaches that the בכור may give up his extra share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift can always be refused. So רבי learns that the בכור may say 'I won't take the extra share, and I won't pay extra toward the debts.' This matches the rule we saw in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: I am not taking (the extra share)
I am not giving (an extra part of the debt)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not giving' does not mean he refuses to give something away from his own share. It means he won't pay a double part of the father's debts, as in step 5.

phrases.english: That teaches that if he says:
'I am not taking and I am not giving,' he is allowed.
phrases.notes: He won't take the extra share of the estate, so he won't pay an extra share of the debts.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לתת לו' limits the share to what the father held.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, 'לתת לו' only teaches that the בכור may refuse the extra share and the extra debt.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use both words. רבי learns the comparison from 'פי שנים' and the right to refuse from 'לתת לו.' The רבנן learn the gift rule from 'לתת לו' and the side-by-side rule from 'פי שנים.'

steps.title: רב פפא: growth everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that when a palm tree gets thicker, or land builds up silt, everyone agrees the בכור takes a double share of the growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: a palm tree that got thicker, or land that built up silt, everyone agrees he takes a double share.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets limits on the argument. First he names cases where even the רבנן agree the בכור gets a double share of the growth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the item stays exactly what it was: the same tree, the same field, just bigger or richer. Since it is still the father's item, even the רבנן count it as something that was in his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Silt, rich soil left by water

steps.confusionAlert: Step 3 said the רבנן give no double share of growth after death. רב פפא shows they still agree when the item itself never changed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
a palm tree that grew thicker,
land that built up silt,
everyone agrees that he takes [a double share].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources to defining which kinds of growth are in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Growth where the item stays the same (a thicker palm tree, land with added silt) gets a double share according to everyone.

steps.title: רב פפא: where they argue, when the item changes form
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about unripe grain that became full ears and date blossoms that became dates. רבי sees this as growth on its own; the רבנן see it as a changed item.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about green grain that became full ears, and date blossoms that became dates. One master holds it is growth that came by itself, and the other holds it has changed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his statement by naming the cases that are really in dispute and giving each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the item turns into something new: blossoms become fruit and green stalks become grain. רבי focuses on the fact that it grew by itself, without the orphans' work, so the בכור gets a double share. The רבנן focus on the change: it is no longer the item the father held, so there is no double share.
steps.whatToRemember: No change in the item means everyone agrees the בכור gets double. A natural change of form is the argument: רבי says double, the רבנן say no.
steps.whyThisMatters: This narrows the מחלוקת from step 3. It is not about every kind of growth after death. It is only about natural growth that turns the item into something new: רבי counts it as growth that came by itself, and the רבנן count it as a changed item.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is green grain that became full ears,
and date blossoms that became dates;
for one master holds: it is growth that came by itself,
and one master holds: it has changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's statement by naming the cases in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about growth where the item changes form. רבי gives a double share because it grew by itself; the רבנן do not, because the item changed.

steps.title: A judge may rule like either side
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנא quotes רבי חייא: if a judge rules like רבי, his ruling stands. If he rules like the חכמים, his ruling also stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנא said in the name of רבי חייא: if a judge acted (ruled) like the words of רבי, what he did stands. If he ruled like the words of the חכמים, what he did also stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling about the argument it just explained: in this case a judge may follow either רבי or the חכמים, and his decision is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13 and 14 explained what רבי and the רבנן argue about: grain or dates that grew after the father died. Usually the גמרא decides whose view is the הלכה. Here רבי חייא says both views are acceptable in practice, so once a judge has ruled either way, nobody can overturn his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted. Here it means a judge ruled. The repeated עָשָׂה means 'what he did stands.'
According to the words (the opinion) of
The Sages, the same group the גמרא earlier called the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: In the argument about a בכור and property that changed after the father's death, the הלכה is not decided for one side. A judge who rules like רבי or like the חכמים has ruled legally, and his ruling stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the second עָשָׂה as 'he did it again.' The repeat means 'what he did is valid,' so his ruling cannot be undone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the רבי and רבנן argument. It tells us a בית דין's decision in such a case is final, whichever opinion it followed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חָנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Ḥiyya said:
If one acted according to the words of Rabbi, what he did stands.
phrases.notes: Here 'acted' means a judge ruled this way in a real case, and his ruling stands.

phrases.english: If he acted according to the words of the Sages, what he did stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חָנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא עָשָׂה כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עָשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 13 and 14 defined exactly where רבי and the רבנן argue, this step gives the practical ruling for that argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who rules like רבי or like the חכמים on the בכור's share of property that improved has ruled validly, and his decision stands.
